nodes.title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks
nodes.note: A slow network learns to write the weights of a fast network on the fly, using outer products of keys and values. The first fast weight programmer.

nodes.title: A 'Self-Referential' Weight Matrix
nodes.note: A recurrent network with special units that address, read and change its own weights, so it could in principle learn its own learning algorithm.

nodes.title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
nodes.note: Brings fast weights back to modern deep learning as a short-term memory for recurrent networks.

nodes.title: HyperNetworks
nodes.note: One network generates the weights of another. A common building block for later work that generates or adapts weights.

nodes.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention
nodes.note: Linear attention turns a transformer into a recurrent model whose state is a sum of key-value outer products.

nodes.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
nodes.note: Shows that linear attention is a fast weight programmer and replaces the additive update with the delta rule.

nodes.title: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
nodes.note: A scalable self-referential weight matrix that generates its own keys, queries and learning rates and rewrites itself with the delta rule.

nodes.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
nodes.note: Makes the hidden state a small model trained by gradient steps while the sequence is read.

nodes.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
nodes.note: Adds gating to delta-rule linear attention. Its state is the memory that later computers-in-weights reuse as exact RAM.

nodes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
nodes.note: A neural long-term memory whose weights are updated during inference.

nodes.title: On the Turing Completeness of Modern Neural Network Architectures
nodes.note: Proves by construction that transformers with hand-set weights can simulate any Turing machine, given enough precision.

nodes.title: Thinking Like Transformers
nodes.note: RASP, a small programming language whose programs map onto attention and MLP layers.

nodes.title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
nodes.note: A compiler that turns RASP programs into real transformer weights, giving models whose circuits are known exactly.

nodes.title: Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
nodes.note: Builds a looped transformer that executes programs given in its input, acting as a general-purpose computer.

nodes.title: Learning Transformer Programs
nodes.note: Trains transformers constrained so that they can be turned back into readable programs.

nodes.title: ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers
nodes.note: A language and compiler with loops, used to ask which algorithms transformers can represent and learn.

nodes.title: Can LLMs Be Computers?
nodes.note: Compiles an interpreter into standard transformer weights analytically, so programs run inside the model at high speed.

nodes.title: torchwright: compiling computation graphs into transformer weights
nodes.note: A compiler from PyTorch-style graphs to vanilla transformer weights; later used to compile a Doom renderer.

nodes.title: Qwenputer: a deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
nodes.note: Compiles a full CPU into extra layers of a production model and uses its Gated DeltaNet state as RAM. Set off a wave of GPUs, filesystems and consoles in weights.

nodes.title: Rewriting a Deep Generative Model
nodes.note: Edits one layer of a GAN as a linear associative memory with a rank-one update, changing a rule the model learned.

nodes.title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
nodes.note: Finds MLP neurons tied to specific facts and edits facts by changing them.

nodes.title: Editing Factual Knowledge in Language Models
nodes.note: Trains a hypernetwork that predicts weight updates to change single facts.

nodes.title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
nodes.note: MEND: small networks turn a fine-tuning gradient into a targeted low-rank edit for large models.

nodes.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
nodes.note: ROME: causal tracing locates facts in mid-layer MLPs, then a closed-form rank-one edit rewrites one fact.

nodes.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
nodes.note: MEMIT scales ROME to thousands of facts edited at once across several layers.

nodes.title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
nodes.note: Averaging the weights of fine-tuned models from one start point often beats picking the best one.

nodes.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
nodes.note: Aligns neurons across independently trained networks so their weights can be merged.

nodes.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
nodes.note: A task vector is fine-tuned weights minus base weights; adding, negating and combining them edits behaviour.

nodes.title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing in Language Models
nodes.note: Finds that where causal tracing locates a fact barely predicts which layer is best to edit.

nodes.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
nodes.note: Trims small changes and resolves sign conflicts before merging task vectors.

nodes.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
nodes.note: Projects edits into the null space of preserved knowledge so new edits disturb less.

nodes.title: Predicting Neural Network Accuracy from Weights
nodes.note: Simple statistics of trained weights predict a network's test accuracy, treating weights as data.

nodes.title: Hyper-Representations: Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Neural Network Weights for Model Characteristic Prediction
nodes.note: Learns embeddings of whole networks from their weights.

nodes.title: Learning to Learn with Generative Models of Neural Network Checkpoints
nodes.note: A diffusion model over checkpoints that outputs parameters reaching a requested loss in one step.

nodes.title: Model Zoos: A Dataset of Diverse Populations of Neural Network Models
nodes.note: Large populations of trained networks released as data for weight-space research.

nodes.title: Equivariant Architectures for Learning in Deep Weight Spaces
nodes.note: Networks that take weights as input and respect the permutation symmetries of neurons.

nodes.title: Permutation Equivariant Neural Functionals
nodes.note: Neural functionals: layers built to process other networks' weights under neuron permutations.

nodes.title: Neural Network Diffusion
nodes.note: Generates working network parameters with a latent diffusion model.

nodes.title: Graph Metanetworks for Processing Diverse Neural Architectures
nodes.note: Represents any network as a graph so one metanetwork can read many architectures.

nodes.title: Towards Scalable and Versatile Weight Space Learning
nodes.note: SANE learns representations of large networks piece by piece and can sample new models.

nodes.title: Reactive optimizers
nodes.note: An agent watches training and rewrites the optimizer's code as training runs.

nodes.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming
nodes.note: A frontier LLM reads small networks' weights, writes game-playing networks, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B to stop reasoning loops.

nodes.title: Does a weight edit teach Qwen3.5-0.8B math, or stop it looping?
nodes.note: Measures the released edit: one direction removed in two layers, tied to repetition. With thinking off the gain is 1.6 points.

nodes.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
nodes.note: Weight reading looks like local arithmetic at the network's edges plus memorised dataset priors.

nodes.title: 4-digit multiplication in 355 nonzero weights with 0 training
nodes.note: An LLM writes every weight of tiny transformers that multiply 4-digit numbers exactly.

nodes.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
nodes.note: 16 editing runs on 0.8B and 9B models: large local gains, uneven transfer, and many runs that keep the original weights.

nodes.title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
nodes.note: Editing 65 embedding rows repairs instruction grounding in a robot policy; the editor rejects most other candidates.

nodes.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
nodes.note: Hand-written networks are provably correct on simple games but collapse where multi-move planning is needed.

nodes.title: WeightProgramBench
nodes.note: Reinforcement learning teaches open models to write game-playing networks, beating Opus on one overfit task.

nodes.title: Weight-space programming: editing Qwen3.5 into a top Pac-Man decision model
nodes.note: Two coding agents edit Qwen3.5 into a Pac-Man decision model by writing a mid-layer probe back into the weights.

nodes.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
nodes.note: Programs built from declared LM modules, then compiled by optimizers that tune prompts, examples, or weights. The 'programming, not prompting' view that weight-space programming later extends to weights.

nodes.title: Handwired: turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net
nodes.note: A compiler from ordinary JavaScript to network weights, with no training and outputs that match the program exactly; runs in the browser.
